title: Couple escapes after lightning strike sparks fire at Yell County home - NewsBreak
text:
By Mike Rogers ,
4 hours ago
OLA, Ark. — What began as a quiet evening quickly turned into a nightmare for James and his wife at their home just outside of Ola, when a lightning strike ignited a fire in their attic, sparking a tense few moments as they scrambled to respond.
The couple had been watching TV as a thunderstorm rolled through the area on Sunday night. James Westlake had dozed off in his recliner when a loud boom shook the house around 8 p.m.
“We both thought it hit something close by. We didn’t think it hit the house,” James said.
Arkansas Storm Team Blog: Warmer & drier October, November & December possible Moments later, they noticed the television had reset itself, and a burning smell began to spread through the house.
“I was messing with the TV and smelled smoke,” he said. “We got up and started checking the house, and when I went out to the back porch, I saw flames coming out of the north end by the garage. That’s when I knew.”
James immediately called 911 while he and his wife rushed to save what they could — loading up their cat and moving their vehicles out of the garage. Rain from the ongoing storm helped slow the flames, but thick smoke made it difficult for the couple and first responders to assess the full extent of the fire at first.
“The firefighters tried to get up here, but it was so full of smoke they couldn’t go in without respirators. They had to wait for the firetruck,” James said.
Thanks to the quick response from local fire crews — and what James called “a blessing” from the rain and foam insulation in the attic — the fire was contained before it could destroy the entire house.
“It’s a setback, but we’re thankful it wasn’t worse,” he said. “The house was on fire. I saw the flames coming through the roof, and at that point, I thought we were going to lose everything.”
Though much of the damage was confined to the attic and garage areas, smoke has affected the rest of the home. Insurance adjusters have already visited, and cleanup is underway.
“They’ll have to tear out the damaged parts and replace it all,” James added. “It’s going to take a few days, maybe weeks.”
The Westlakes have owned the property for more than a decade, but the home itself is just three years old — a dream project for James’ wife.
“It was her dream home,” he said. “But they’ll get it fixed up, and hopefully one day we won’t even be able to tell this happened.”
Arkansas Storm Team Blog: Humberto joins Gabrielle in the Atlantic & another wave to watch Looking ahead, the couple says they’re considering adding a lightning rod to the roof, given the home’s remote location and lack of nearby tall structures.
“We’re sitting out in the middle of nowhere,” James said. “There’s nothing around us, so we’re thinking about it now.”
For now, the couple is focused on cleanup and moving forward.
“We’re blessed that it didn’t burn the house down,” James said. “We’ll get through it.”
